data.name: Shivraj
data.gender_notes: Shivraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Shivraj is a name of Lord Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction and regeneration. The name Shivraj means 'ruler of Shiva' or 'ruler of the universe'. The name Shivraj carries the meaning “Lord Shiva, Ruler” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shivraj usually hope their child will grow to embody lord shiva, ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shivraj is a name of Lord Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction and regeneration. It represents the power and strength of Lord Shiva, as well as his role as the ruler of the universe. The name Shivraj is a reminder of the cyclical nature of life and the importance of destruction and renewal in the natural order of things.
data.etymology: Shivraj belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Shiva, Ruler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shivraj total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shivraj carries great importance in Hindu culture as it represents the supreme power and reign of Lord Shiva. It is a sign of strength, power, and authority. This name is often given to children born during significant Hindu festivals dedicated to Lord Shiva or duringauspicious occasions.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, Shivraj represents the divine power and mastery of Lord Shiva over the Universe and its Laws. It signifies a deep connection with the divine, and those who bear this name are believed to have the blessings and protection of Lord Shiva, who is also considered the destroyer of negative energies. It is a reminder that even in destruction, there is creation and renewal, a fundamental principle of the universe.

historical_references.reference: Shivaji Bhonsle was a Hindu warrior-king who ruled the Maratha Confederacy from 1630 to 1680. He is considered a legendary figure for his military and administrative prowess, and is a symbol of Hindu nationalism in India.
The name 'Shivaji' translates to 'Lord Shiva's light'. Shivaji Bhonsle took this name to signify his devotion to Lord Shiva, who is considered one of the major Hindu deities.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shivraj' is derived from Hindu mythology, where Shiva is referred to as the 'Raj' or the king. In modern contexts, this name is seen on various platforms. In social media, there are numerous profiles, groups and pages dedicated to Lord Shiva, with 'Shivraj' being a common name used. In the music industry, there are several songs, albums and artists named after Shivraj, such as the Indian classical music album 'Shivraj Stotra'. Lastly, in literature, there are books, poems and essays written about Shivraj and his significance in Hinduism.
